secao: Lecture VI: Carbon Or Charcoal—Coal-Gas—Respiration And Its Analogy To The Burning Of A Candle—Conclusion.
titulo: Lecture VI: Carbon Or Charcoal—Coal-Gas—Respiration And Its Analogy To The Burning Of A Candle—Conclusion.
textoOriginal: If, when the carbon burnt, the product went off as a solid body, you would have had the room filled with an opaque substance, as in the case of the phosphorus; but when carbon burns, everything passes up into the atmosphere. It is in a fixed, almost unchangeable condition before the combustion; but afterwards it is in the form of gas, which it is very difficult (though we have succeeded) to produce in a solid or a liquid state.
